title: I Let the Squash-Court Light Timer Catch the League Who Overstayed

parts.text: I booked court 4 at 8:00 p.m. At 8:04 the league was still on with the lights they had set to a 90-minute override. The light-timer policy they voted for said: 45 MINUTES. NO OVERRIDES AFTER LEAGUE. I was thirty-eight, recreational, holding a key fob. League captain Mo said, "Sudden death." I pointed at the vote printout. They served. "Death doesn't fob." I photographed the override panel, the printout, and the 8:04 clock. Then I let the front desk remote-reset the timer as the policy allowed. At 8:06 the court went dark and the desk asked why Mo's name was on an override ticket.
parts.cliffhanger_hint: The desk can see a 90-minute override against the 45-minute vote Mo backed.

social.video_title: League kept a 90-minute light override — Part 1/2
social.description: 8:00 fob, sudden death, and a vote printout. The desk reset the timer. Would you have stretched in the dark?

parts.text: Mo called it a rally until the panel log showed the override code. I printed the ticket, the vote, and the photo. Lights came back on my booking. Mo told the gallery the vote was always about optics. Optics is a word leagues use when a court goes dark. Timer policy now has a second line: SUDDEN DEATH ENDS AT 45. I play. Mo showers. The bulb finally respects the fob.

social.description: Override ticket, lights on my booking, and a second line on the vote. Was a rally ever 90 minutes of someone else's court?
